newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken has no comment on foreign interest talk.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken has no comment on foreign interest talk.

text.p: The chairman of Sweden's state-controlled Nordbanken, Jacob Palmstierna, declined to comment on Wednesday on a report in a Swedish newspaper that an overseas bank was interested in buying the bank.
Asked if there was any truth to the report, Palmstierna said: "I think I will refrain from comment.
"This is the rule in such a case anyway. It is not that I want to be difficult but I cannot comment."
Financial daily Finanstidningen said on Wednesday that a foreign bank had approached the Swedish government, showing interest in buying the bank which is 59 percent state owned.
"According to other information, not yet confirmed, an insurance company also has shown interest in some kind of coordination with Nordbanken," Finanstidningen added.
Merger talks between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken failed in early February.
The banks did not give any reason for the failure, but analysts said S-E-Banken's management could not accept that Nordbanken wanted both the chief executive and chairman posts.
Nordbanken's chief executive, the government and S-E-Banken owners have said they are sorry the deal did not go through and market players are speculating on another round of merger talks.
Nordbanken's share were four crowns lower at 270 crowns at 1450 GMT and S-E-Banken shares down two at 80.
